headline: Failed Senate resolution would have required the President to remove U.S. troops from hostilities against Iran unless Congress authorized them.
what_it_does: This resolution would have directed the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Iran. The troops would have been allowed to stay involved only if Congress passed a declaration of war or a specific authorization to use military force. It would not have stopped the United States from defending itself, its personnel, or its facilities abroad from an attack. On April 30, 2026, the Senate refused to take it up or end debate on it, so it did not pass.

who_it_affects.how: Those taking part in hostilities in or against Iran would have been withdrawn unless Congress approved the military action.
The President would have needed a declaration of war or an authorization from Congress to keep U.S. forces in hostilities against Iran, except to defend against attacks.
Congress would have had to vote to approve any continued U.S. military hostilities against Iran.
